acceptance: Each of SSB, TPC-DI and the three primitives has a recorded SF 100 result: completed with time and size, or the largest practical scale with the reason.
Any proposal to change a maximum is recorded as a separate item.
context: Created 2026-11-11 to re-home the large-scale validation that was narrowed out of scale-factor-registry-caps-vs-docs-20261013.
description:
## Problem
The scale-factor rule now accepts any value up to 100000 with a note, but no run shows that the pure-Python generators (SSB, TPC-DI) finish at large scales, or that the primitives, which run on TPC-H data (`data_source: tpch`), complete at SF 100. `scale-factor-registry-caps-vs-docs-20261013` originally required generator validation at the new scales; that part moved here when the owner chose the range rule on 2026-11-11.

## Change
Run data generation at SF 100 for SSB and TPC-DI, and a read, write and transaction primitives run at SF 100, through `make heavy-run`. Record time, row counts and output size. If a generator cannot finish in a practical time, record the largest practical scale and propose either a faster generator or a lower registry maximum.

## Guardrails
- Heavy runs only through `make heavy-run`, with the memory budget the owner approves for the run. SF 100 TPC-H data is about 100 GB: confirm free disk before starting and write under `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR`.
- No registry change in this item; a lower maximum is a separate decision.
